content:
Morgan: incident-bot alerted: major drop in throughput for runtime-pool-A in us-east-1
perf-bot: auto alert: throughput -55% over 10m, p50 +180ms, p95 +1.0s
Morgan: seeing repeated GPU OOMs on a subset of workers, getting restarts
Ravi: pulling logs and NVML dumps now
Ravi: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/runtime-pool-a -c worker --since=15m | grep -i oom` => several 'CUDA out of memory' entries
Aisha: noisy-tenants report: spike in other GPU jobs coincident with the incident window
Tom: checking host dmesg and cgroup kills
Tom: `dmesg | egrep -i "Out of memory|Killed process"` shows the worker process being killed by OOM killer on hosts 10-13
Morgan: profiler traces: heavy KV cache growth for long chats — many requests with prefix >7k tokens
Morgan: KV cache not properly trimmed when workers restart due to eviction race; caches accumulate before GC
Ravi: kernel selection logs: started with optimized_attention_fp16 then fell back to fallback_attention_fp32 under memory pressure
Ravi: fallback kernel uses ~2.5-2.8x more transient memory per token — explains throughput collapse after fallbacks
Aisha: also noticed config change earlier today that bumped auto-batcher max batch from 16->32
Tom: that could raise instantaneous memory demand; combining with large prefixes is risky
Morgan: immediate mitigations: roll AUTOBATCH_MAX_BATCH down to 8 and disable prefix caching for huge sessions
Morgan: ran `kubectl set env deploy/runtime-pool-a AUTOBATCH_MAX_BATCH=8 PREFIX_CACHE_ENABLED=false` as canary on 4/8 pods
perf-bot: canary rollout in progress on 4/8 pods
Ravi: canary pods show immediate p50/p95 improvement; non-canary pods unchanged
Tom: observed frequent worker restarts; each restart leaves small GPU allocations for ~20-40s before driver fully reclaims -> fragmentation
Ravi: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` shows many small free holes across GPUs on impacted hosts
Aisha: plan: 1) throttle other noisy tenant jobs on these hosts, 2) finish config roll to all pods, 3) schedule node reboots if fragmentation persists
Morgan: question: is a driver reset enough or do we need full node reboots? GCP limits gpu reset in some images
Tom: tried restarting nvidia-persistenced and driver modules — didn't free the tiny fragments reliably; kernel-level reset or reboot is safer
Ravi: found a kernel-selection regression: quantized kernels being selected for sequences >2048 tokens; they allocate large temporaries and blow past expected memory caps
Ravi: patch branch available: fix/kernel-selection-length-guard, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/433
Aisha: logged action items in INC-2026-022: throttle tenants, roll config, merge kernel guard, schedule node reboots overnight if needed
Ravi: added temporary circuit-breaker: if OOM_rate > 3/min then reject new long-prefix sessions (503) to avoid cascading failures
Morgan: will roll the config to remaining pods once CI passes; monitor `requests/sec`, `p99`, `gpu.memory_fragmentation` metric, and `worker.restart_rate`
Tom: follow-ups: add a unit test for kernel selection length guard and a memory churn regression test in CI
Ravi: also adding a probe for autoscaler to consider contiguous GPU free memory (not just total free)
perf-bot: canary -> full rollout complete; throughput recovered ~40% vs worst-case on impacted pods
Aisha: scheduling node reboots for two heavily fragmented hosts at 02:30-03:30 UTC to fully defragment if metrics don't normalize
Morgan: incident declared mitigated; postmortem owner assigned to Ravi, due in 72h
Morgan: thanks for quick responses — keep any traces or heap profiles here if you find more evidence of big temporaries
Aisha: uploaded `/tmp/profiles/worker-11-large-prefix.heap` with repeated allocations from attention_kv_cache::reserve
Ravi: merging kernel-selection guard PR now and will watch release metrics
Morgan: closing incident channel for now; will reopen if regressions reappear :white_check_mark:
